title: Bus plunges into ravine in fog near Talagang; 5 dead, 27 hurt
detail: A Rawalpindi-Multan bus lost control on a foggy mountain road near Dhok Pathan and fell about 100 feet into a ravine; Rescue 1122 reported 5 dead and 27 injured. Motorways M-1 to M-5 and M-14 were closed for fog, diverting traffic to GT Road.

title: BLA coordinated attacks across Quetta and nine Balochistan districts
detail: BLA claimed coordinated attacks on military, police and government sites in Quetta and nine districts; Al Jazeera reported 15 security personnel and 18 civilians killed, and officials claimed 92 BLA fighters killed in 48 hours. Train and internet services were suspended.
attribution: Toll per officials cited by Al Jazeera; militant toll is a government claim; BLA claimed responsibility

title: Gul Plaza mall fire in Karachi kills at least 28
detail: A mid-January night fire at Karachi's Gul Plaza shopping mall killed at least 28; firefighters told a commissioner-led inquiry that locked grill doors and blocked stairways trapped occupants. The cause was still under investigation.

title: Suicide bombing at Islamabad mosque during Friday prayers
detail: A bombing at Khadija Al-Kubra mosque on the outskirts of Islamabad during Friday prayers killed at least 31 and wounded 169; there was no immediate claim.
attribution: Toll per officials cited by Euronews

title: Pakistan launches Operation Ghazab lil Haq against Afghan Taliban
detail: Pakistan's military launched Operation Ghazab lil Haq late on 26 February after renewed cross-border clashes. By 7 March Information Minister Attaullah Tarar claimed 527 Afghan Taliban killed, 755 injured, 237 posts destroyed and 38 captured; figures not independently verified.
attribution: Casualty figures are claims by Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, reported by The Express Tribune (7 Mar 2026)

title: Pro-Iran protesters storm US consulate Karachi; deadly unrest
detail: After the killing of Iran's Supreme Leader in US-Israeli strikes, protesters tried to storm the US consulate in Karachi; at least 10 killed and over 70 wounded there, and 7 killed in Gilgit-Baltistan, with a UN office burned in Skardu.
attribution: Tolls per officials/rescue services cited by Al Jazeera and AFP

title: Over 500 flights cancelled in three days over regional war
detail: Pakistan Airports Authority data showed over 500 domestic and international flights cancelled over three days at Lahore, Karachi, Islamabad, Peshawar, Quetta, Faisalabad and Multan as Gulf airspaces closed.

title: Taftan trade disrupted, prices soar as Pakistanis flee Iran war
detail: Pakistanis were returning via Taftan after US-Israeli strikes on Iran; with the crossing's trade disrupted, local food and fuel prices reportedly doubled or tripled and PM Shehbaz Sharif ordered contingency measures.
attribution: Local accounts reported by Pakistan TV

title: Coast Guards and Navy seize $110m of drugs in Jiwani hills
detail: Pakistan Coast Guards and Navy seized 1,050 kg hashish and 200 kg methamphetamine hidden in the Jiwani mountains awaiting sea shipment, valued at about $110 million.

title: Navy launches Operation Muhafiz-ul-Bahr to protect shipping
detail: ISPR said the Pakistan Navy launched Operation Muhafiz-ul-Bahr to counter threats to national shipping and sea lines amid the Iran war; at launch Navy ships were escorting two merchant vessels with PNSC.

title: Emergency austerity as Iran war triggers fuel crisis
detail: PM Shehbaz Sharif ordered a four-day week for government staff, two-week school closures from 16 March and cuts in fuel use as Hormuz disruption hit oil supply; petrol rose about 20% in a week.

title: FIA-SBP joint working group formed against hawala-hundi
detail: Government formed an FIA-State Bank joint working group co-chaired by Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb to act against illegal cross-border fund transfers.

title: 10,619 people return from Iran via Taftan since war began
detail: FIA said 10,619 passengers arrived at Taftan between 28 February and 8 April 2026 as the Iran war disrupted the region; FIA deployed round-the-clock immigration staff.
attribution: Figures from the Federal Investigation Agency

title: SBP lifts seven-year ban on banks serving licensed crypto firms
detail: State Bank allowed banks to open accounts for PVARA-licensed virtual asset providers while barring them from trading or holding crypto, with enhanced due diligence and AML/CFT monitoring required.
attribution: SBP circular as reported by CoinDesk

title: KP puts hospitals on high alert as mpox cases reach 26
detail: The KP Health Department ordered all hospitals to isolate suspected mpox cases and step up surveillance after 26 confirmed infections over 12 months, warning of local transmission.

title: FIA seizes over Rs250m at Chakdara in hawala raid
detail: FIA arrested two suspects at Chakdara toll plaza and recovered over Rs250 million allegedly moved via unlicensed hawala/hundi.

title: Suicide car bomb hits Quetta shuttle train at Chaman Phatak
detail: A vehicle-borne suicide bomb struck the Quetta Cantonment-railway station shuttle train near Chaman Phatak, derailing three coaches; Dawn's early report gave 14 dead (incl. 3 FC personnel) and 20 injured, later reports put the toll far higher. CM Sarfraz Bugti blamed 'Fitna al Hindustan'.
attribution: Early toll per officials cited by Dawn; BLA reportedly claimed

title: Police and peace committee kill 25 militants in Bannu clash
detail: Bannu's district police officer said more than 25 militants, including two commanders, were killed in fighting in Barakzai Akhundkhel, Miryan tehsil; two police and two civilians died and 10 were injured. A 10 kg remote-controlled bomb near a mosque was defused.

title: Power shortfall hits 6,500 MW; rural load-shedding up to 16 hours
detail: Express Tribune reported demand near 22,000 MW against 15,400 MW supply, with 3-8 hour urban and 8-16 hour rural outages; a Petroleum Division official blamed halted LNG cargoes, and the Power Division cited a 1,991 MW drop in hydropower.

title: Dadu hits record 51.5C as Sindh heatwave peaks
detail: PMD recorded 51.5C at Dadu, 4.5C above normal; Larkana and Jacobabad hit 50.5C, with 47-50C forecast across upper Sindh.

title: Bannu police repel pre-dawn assault on Mazanga post; 6 attackers killed
detail: Express Tribune reported police repelled an armed pre-dawn assault on the Mazanga police post early on a Wednesday, killing at least six attackers; one constable was lightly injured and weapons and grenades were recovered.

title: FBR designates Taftan railway station a land customs station
detail: FBR notification SRO1055/2026 designated the 11.75-acre Taftan railway station as a land customs station for Pakistan-Iran trade, aiming to curb informal trade channels.

title: Glacier melt floods hit Nagar, Ghanche, Ghizer; GLOF alert
detail: Heatwave-driven glacier melt flooded Hoper and Hisper valleys (Nagar), Ghanche and Ghizer, submerging a Hushe suspension bridge and briefly blocking the KKH near Khunjerab; NDMA issued a GLOF alert.

title: DG ISPR: 38 killed in three Balochistan attacks over four days
detail: DG ISPR Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said attacks 4-8 July (Hanna Urak, Ziarat checkpoint, Bela-Winder convoy ambush) killed 4 civilians, 27 police and 7 soldiers, and claimed 54 militants killed; he alleged Indian backing and Afghan nationals among attackers.
attribution: Claims by DG ISPR reported by Dawn

title: FIA arrests suspect over families of Pakistanis missing in Iran
detail: FIA arrested a suspect in Gujrat allegedly in a network that took money from families of 12 Pakistanis missing in Iran with false promises of travel to Europe; another held for French work-visa fraud.

title: TTP-linked suicide vehicle attack on Tank check post kills 15
detail: ISPR said militants assaulted a joint police check post in Tank and detonated an explosive-laden vehicle overnight 23/24 July, killing 12 soldiers, 2 policemen and a forest official; ISPR claimed 12 attackers killed.
attribution: ISPR statement; militants described by ISPR as 'Fitna al Khawarij' (TTP)

title: Monsoon toll passes 100; Lahore-Gujranwala plains inundated
detail: NDMA said 107 killed and 344 injured since late June (KP 55, Punjab 36); about 400 sq km under water in Lahore and Gujranwala divisions and 17 relief camps set up in Lahore.
attribution: NDMA figures; cumulative national toll placed at Lahore

title: Quadcopter-and-gun attack on Hangu police post kills 11 officers
detail: Attackers used explosive-laden quadcopters before storming a police checkpoint in Hangu, killing 11 officers including a deputy superintendent and wounding 28; police said 15 attackers were killed. No claim.
attribution: Figures from District Police Officer Mujahid Hussain via Al Jazeera

title: Suicide bomber hits Kabal police station in Swat; 17 dead
detail: A suicide bomber blew himself up at the Kabal police station entrance as officers moved to search him, while a protest against lawlessness was under way nearby; 7 police and 10 civilians died and 27 were injured. No claim was reported.

title: NDMA warns heavy rain, hill torrents; toll 126
detail: NDMA warned of heavy to very heavy rain through 4 August with flash-flood risk in DG Khan hill torrents and urban flooding in Lahore, Rawalpindi, Gujranwala, Hyderabad; season toll 126 since 26 June.

title: 144 Karachi children dead from measles and diphtheria since January
detail: Hospital data reported by Dawn showed 1,915 measles cases with 125 deaths and 81 diphtheria cases with 19 deaths in Karachi in the first seven months of 2026; the Sindh EPI director said measles cases were down 35% on 2025.

title: GLOF and cloudburst cut off Chitral, two dead
detail: Glacial outburst and a cloudburst hit valleys across Upper and Lower Chitral, killing two, destroying about a dozen bridges in Karimabad, cutting the Chitral-Peshawar and Chitral-Shandur roads and internet; over 150 vehicles stranded.

title: 258 foreigners held in Islamabad scam call centre raid
detail: FIA detained 258 foreign nationals (about 40 Chinese, 170 Vietnamese, plus Malaysians and others) at a call centre in Gulberg Green allegedly running Ponzi/investment fraud; they had entered on tourist visas.
attribution: FIA figures reported by ProPakistani; raid 'last week' before 17 Aug

title: NCCIA raids 'Aofu Group' centre in I-10, 276 foreigners arrested
detail: NCCIA arrested 276 foreigners at an I-10/3 facility operating as 'Aofu Group', alleged to lure victims into sexual video chats, impersonation and cheating; FIR under PECA 2016.

title: Pakistan to blacklist 671 foreigners held in call centre raids
detail: FIA will blacklist 671 foreign nationals arrested in call centre raids and the government approved an FIA-led nationwide task force, with focus on Karachi; offences alleged include fraud, blackmail, gambling and live-streamed explicit content.
attribution: FIA decision reported by Daily Pakistan

title: Punjab load-shedding returns as national shortfall tops 4,000 MW
detail: Express Tribune reported a national shortfall over 4,000 MW and over 1,200 MW in LESCO's area, with Lahore residents facing hour-on, hour-off cuts after a failed RLNG cargo delivery reduced plant output.

title: FIA deports 20 more Chinese nationals in I-10 call centre case
detail: FIA deported 20 Chinese nationals linked to the I-10 call centre (34 deported in the case, incl. 14 Vietnamese earlier) and blacklisted them; charges under Foreigners Act and PECA.
attribution: FIA figures reported by The Nation

title: ANF-DEA seize 463kg crystal meth bound for Colombo
detail: ANF with US DEA and Sri Lanka police seized about 463 kg of crystal methamphetamine in containers to be shipped from Pakistan to Colombo, worth about $21 million (Rs5.8bn); several suspects arrested.
attribution: DEA/ANF statement reported by The Nation; exact seizure site not given

title: KP dengue cases reach 478 for 2026, led by Peshawar and Kohat
detail: The KP Health Department's disease surveillance system reported 478 confirmed dengue cases this year (83 in the past week) out of 2,697 suspected, with Peshawar 177 and Kohat 151; no deaths reported.

title: 150mm downpour floods Islamabad; Nullah Lai at dangerous level
detail: About 150 mm fell in Islamabad's E-11; Nullah Lai rose to dangerous levels and Rawalpindi declared a holiday. NDMA put the season toll (26 Jun-31 Aug) at 175 (KP 70, Punjab 61, Sindh 17).
attribution: Rainfall and toll per NDMA/PMD via Arab News

title: ANF seizes 364.6kg of narcotics worth Rs2.12bn in eight operations
detail: ANF reported eight operations incl. Peshawar airport, Sangjani toll plaza (52.8 kg hashish, 5.4 kg opium) and Lahore, seizing narcotics worth over Rs2.12 billion and arresting eight.

title: Fire collapses half of a Landhi EPZ factory in Karachi
detail: Rescue 1122 said a blaze at a used-clothing factory in the Landhi Export Processing Zone engulfed the building and caused about half of it to collapse, damaging an adjacent factory; 16 fire tenders responded and three workers had minor injuries.

title: Fourth polio case of 2026 confirmed in Bannu
detail: NEOC confirmed a wild poliovirus case in Nurar UC, Miryan tehsil, Bannu, bringing 2026 cases to four (KP 3, Sindh 1); three are from southern KP where security limits vaccinator access.

title: FIA probes alleged Rs172bn laundering by Islamabad call centre network
detail: FIA is investigating about Rs172 billion allegedly moved through bank and microfinance accounts and sent abroad by the call centre network; a nine-member JIT was formed and 50 Vietnamese detainees deported.
attribution: FIA allegations reported by Daily Pakistan

title: Car bomb and assault on Kohat Police Lines kill 23
detail: Attackers detonated a vehicle bomb near the police lines mosque during Friday prayers and stormed the compound; KP police said 17 police and 6 civilians died, over 100 were hurt and 8 attackers were killed in an overnight clearance. Hafiz Gul Bahadur's Ittehadul Mujahideen claimed it; later reports put the toll at 31.

title: Two officers among six soldiers killed in Hangu convoy ambush
detail: ISPR said a convoy came under attack in Hangu district, killing six soldiers including a captain and a lieutenant; ISPR claimed eight 'Fitna al-Khawarij' militants killed.
attribution: ISPR statement reported by The Express Tribune

title: NCCIA raids three E-11/G-10 call centres, 212 held
detail: NCCIA raided three call centres in Islamabad's E-11 and G-10, detaining 212 including seven Chinese nationals, over Google-related, loan, dating and trading frauds; 306 phones and 383 computers seized, links alleged to networks in India and Brazil.
attribution: NCCIA claims reported by The Express Tribune

title: Pakistani air strikes on Afghan provinces after alleged drone incursions
detail: Al Jazeera reported Pakistani strikes on about 10 locations in Kandahar, Paktia and Khost after Islamabad alleged Afghan drone incursions; Kabul denied launching drones and vowed an 'appropriate response', threatening mediation by China, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and Turkmenistan.
attribution: Strike details are Pakistani claims and Afghan government statements reported by Al Jazeera

title: Pakistan says 13 Afghan Taliban killed in Gulistan sector clash
detail: Pakistan's Information Ministry said an attempted Afghan incursion in the Gulistan sector was repulsed overnight 24/25 September, claiming at least 13 Afghan Taliban personnel killed; Kabul denied the claim.
attribution: Claim by Pakistan's Ministry of Information and Broadcasting; Kabul denied (per Geo/AP reporting)
